overview: This single-page Department of State filing list inventories three papers concerning copper and industrial targets in wartime Japan. Its entries describe the sale to Japan of copper held by Italians after Italy entered the war; information on Japanese copper mines, an electrolytic refinery, and a Sumitomo smelter; a photograph taken by Wilton A. Higgins; a Montreal report concerning bombing targets supplied by Thomas Underhill of U.S. Steel in Asia; and an otherwise undescribed 1942 paper associated with George Walker.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on copper in Japan
subfiles.about: A filing inventory summarizes three papers concerning Japanese copper facilities, wartime copper transfers, and bombing-target intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Form DS-46 lists papers numbered 6 through 8 under the subject “Copper--Japan.” Paper 6 concerns copper held by Italians and sold to Japan, information about Japanese mines and processing facilities, and a photograph of a Sumitomo smelter by Wilton A. Higgins. Paper 7 is Montreal telegram No. 4319, associated with Byington, reporting information on bombing targets supplied by Thomas Underhill of U.S. Steel in Asia. Paper 8 identifies only George Walker and the year 1942, without a stated purport.

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact guide to related records that may not survive in this bundle, preserving their dates, origins, and subjects. It links economic intelligence on Japan’s copper industry with Allied target identification and wartime transfers of Italian-held copper. The reference to a photograph of a Sumitomo smelter is especially valuable because it points to visual intelligence, while the incomplete George Walker entry highlights a gap that could guide further archival research.
